findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py:1036–1048 computes carried gates only when proven != expected_head, then publishes the superseding admission before publishing its review-pending record. If execution fails after that admission comment but before the transition at lines 1070–1071, retry sees proven == expected_head and skips gate carry-forward. The recovery transition uses only the fresh handoff gates with inherit_identity=False, dropping the prior passed review. This contradicts the active completion-lifecycle requirement that the new review-pending record SHALL keep every reusable recorded gate and complete review without launching a reviewer.
findings.summary: An interrupted superseding admission loses the reusable review gate when retried, causing a new reviewer run for unchanged task content.
